races.name: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Baila Conmigo
runners_data.note: Strong flat form at a mile-plus in varied ground including a win on Soft/Average, but a natural hold-up operator whose style is compromised here — in a race with few genuine pace-makers, getting into a rhythm behind the pack may not be straightforward.

runners_data.name: Hinchinbrooke
runners_data.note: Has twice been placed over similar distances on Good in Britain and is suited to the trip, but a genuine rear-of-field racer who will likely find himself in a crowded midfield group rather than his natural berth — the limited pace makes his task harder.

runners_data.name: Puppet Master
runners_data.note: Nine outings on Good ground show he handles the surface, but nine runners home in similar fields is a recurring theme; Ciaran Murphy has three wins from 13 runners over 14 days which is a live yard angle worth noting.

runners_data.name: Kimi De Mai
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the ride for the powerful Mullins yard (11/29 in 14 days) on a horse with placed flat form on Heavier ground — a step down to Good on 2m is worth monitoring, though the prominent style suits this pace shape well.

runners_data.name: Charles The Bold
runners_data.note: Holds a 'fades in finish' flag and has only one run on Good going (ninth over 19f), suggesting this trip and surface combination is untested at the required level; held up by nature but will be stranded in an awkward midfield spot in this shape.

runners_data.name: First Ascent
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy from Gordon Elliott's active yard (4/38 in 14 days) provides a strong jockey-trainer angle; four places from eight Good-ground runs shows reliability, and his prominent style is the ideal profile for this sole front-runner scenario.

runners_data.name: Grabat
runners_data.note: Two runs in Ireland both on Good, finishing sixth and eleventh, offer little encouragement; a natural hold-up type pushed into a midfield map position that is not his comfort zone, and Philip Fenton's yard is quiet (0/2 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Jodoro
runners_data.note: Mixed profile with pulled-up and unseated runs in recent form, and no wins from seven Good-ground efforts; a hold-up racer who has struggled to deliver and has been absent 46 days — stamina questions linger.

runners_data.name: Le Roi Arthur
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who can set every fraction at his own discretion on Good ground at Kilbeggan; fell on his most recent start, but third on Good over 18f before that suggests he has the stamina for this trip — the uncontested lead is a significant tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Anns Getaway
runners_data.note: Carrying a 'fades in finish' flag and both Good-ground runs produced mid-teen finishes; a hold-up horse whose redistribution into midfield on the map reflects the congestion at the rear, and her record gives little reason to expect improvement.

runners_data.name: Mistakenforanother
runners_data.note: Four runs on Good going with a second and a fourth among them — shows some ability at this level; a hold-up type who could creep into contention if the race develops in stages, though no wins from four similar-ground attempts is a concern.

runners_data.name: Rene's Gold
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and carries 'fades in finish' and 'lightly raced' flags; Ross O'Sullivan has one winner from 13 over 14 days and the style is unknown enough that this horse is hard to position confidently in any scenario.

runners_data.name: Rose Mountain
runners_data.note: Four Good-ground runs all finishing between ninth and sixteenth, plus a 'fades in finish' tag — the evidence points firmly against; a hold-up racer with no obvious tactical edge in this shape.

runners_data.name: Really Truly
runners_data.note: J J Slevin rides for the in-form Joseph Patrick O'Brien yard (7/57 in 14 days), but one run on Good shows an eleventh-place finish; the 'fades in finish' flag and limited data make her a speculative entry at best.

runners_data.name: Rickety Kate
runners_data.note: A Joseph Patrick O'Brien debutant with no public form data; the stable's exceptional 14-day strike rate (7/57) keeps her in the conversation for the shock scenario, but going and style are entirely unknown quantities.

runners_data.name: Loadstone
runners_data.note: Another O'Brien first-timer with no historical data to analyse; shares the yard's current form angle but carries lightly-raced uncertainty — in a field this size, unknown profiles can land, but it is impossible to place her in a pace scenario with confidence.

runners_data.name: Geashill Poet
runners_data.note: Adrian Murray's debutant with no public record; the trainer runs at 1/3 in the 14-day window which is a modest but live angle — as with the O'Brien unknowns, the pace and going profile are entirely absent.

races.paceDynamic: Le Roi Arthur is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner maiden hurdle and, critically, has no identified rival willing or able to seriously contest the lead — he will stride into the early sections at Kilbeggan on Good ground essentially unchallenged. With a single pace-setter controlling tempo from the front, this creates a classically sustainable, even-gallop scenario where Le Roi Arthur can dictate every yard of the 2m trip without burning energy fighting for position. That controlled, uncontested lead strongly favours prominent racers who can track closely and pounce over the final flight, rather than deep closers who need a true pace to chase down. The field contains substantially more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Hinchinbrooke, Grabat, Charles The Bold, Anns Getaway and Baila Conmigo are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning the runners most likely to secure a natural close-tracking position behind Le Roi Arthur are Kimi De Mai and First Ascent, who should enjoy an uncluttered prominent berth and are best-placed to exploit the controlled pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Le Roi Arthur Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Le Roi Arthur bowls along at a measured clip and no rival has the inclination or ability to press him for the lead.
scenarios.body: Le Roi Arthur controls every stride on easy terms, conserving energy through the back, and the race becomes a test of quality over the final two hurdles rather than stamina; Kimi De Mai and First Ascent, tracking close throughout, are perfectly positioned to mount an immediate challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Le Roi Arthur slightly overdoes it early and a well-placed prominent type has enough in reserve to collar him on the run-in.
scenarios.body: The steady gallop suits horses that can travel smoothly in second or third, switch off, and produce a clean jump at the last to seal the race; First Ascent's Gordon Elliott/Jack Kennedy combination and Kimi De Mai's Mullins-stable form make them the logical beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively slow in the early stages and a midfield runner finds an unobstructed run to exploit a tiring front group.
scenarios.body: Puppet Master has shown consistent Good-ground form and, despite being a hold-up type mapped to midfield, could find a clear passage if the field strings out; Hinchinbrooke also has solid placed form in similar conditions and could emerge late if gaps appear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Lands Shock
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up types fail to find their natural position and the race collapses into a muddled finish that a lightly-raced unexposed type can exploit.
scenarios.body: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's debutants Rickety Kate or Loadstone arrive with unknown profiles but the stable is firing (7/57 over 14 days), and maiden hurdles regularly produce surprise winners from unknown quantities; Geashill Poet also enters with a blank slate.

watchPoints.text: Le Roi Arthur (Kieren Buckley) set the early tempo unchallenged — if he jumps cleanly at the first two hurdles and settles, he could prove very hard to peg back from the front given there is no identified challenger for the lead.

First Ascent and Kimi De Mai are both likely to compete for the same close-tracking position behind Le Roi Arthur — watch for any crowding or interference between them approaching the first turn, as their race may depend on securing that ground.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types — Hinchinbrooke, Grabat, Charles The Bold, Anns Getaway and Baila Conmigo — will all be jostling for space in a congested midfield from the outset; any stumbling or interference in that group could compromise several runners simultaneously.

Joseph Patrick O'Brien's three debutants (Rickety Kate, Loadstone, Really Truly) merit a watch in the market — the yard is striking at 7/57 over 14 days and first-time-out maiden hurdle winners from powerful stables can arrive unannounced.

Good ground is confirmed across all Kilbeggan races today with no variation, meaning no runner gains or loses an unexpected going edge — the surface assessment is stable and reliable for the entire card.

races.name: Follow Kilbeggan On Instagram Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Facile Ocean
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a consistent profile of hitting the frame; trainer Ciaran Murphy sends her in decent nick 13 days since her last run, and five runs on similar going yield a win and four placings — a horse that finishes races and will be handed any pace collapse gift on a plate.

runners_data.name: Magico
runners_data.note: Mullins' stable form is strong (11/29 in 14 days) and this 5-year-old has won over similar going, but 76 days off the track is a fitness question mark; prominent style suits the expected race shape, though his flat-track flat-racing background makes the longer 2m3f trip an open question.

runners_data.name: No Mon No Fun
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on Good most recently and clearly handles this trip and going combination; Jack Doyle's runner has shown a prominent style and with just two hurdle runs in the book he remains lightly tested but his form figures of 1-4 are encouraging at this level.

runners_data.name: Rosie's Wings
runners_data.note: The sole genuine front-runner in the field and likely to bowl along in front unchallenged; her Good-ground record spans six runs and includes a win and three places, and Danny Gilligan should be able to dictate the entire shape of this race from the front on her terms.

runners_data.name: Mino Des Mottes
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy booked for this Gordon Elliott 4-year-old is a significant positive; has a strong record of placing in every completed start with wins at 16f and 17f on Good, and his prominent style is ideal for a race where he can sit just behind Rosie's Wings and attack from the second-last.

runners_data.name: La Cote Fleurie
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's mare has won twice over longer trips on Good ground and her form figures of 1-3-1 in three jumps starts are outstanding; 85 days since last run is worth noting, but the class and finishing pattern she has shown make her a major player if she returns in similar form.

runners_data.name: Eaglewood
runners_data.note: OR 93 and modest recent form aside, the real issue here is that despite being a naturally prominent-racing horse, the congested field pushes him back into midfield where he is racing out of his comfort zone — his style fit in this configuration is compromised and his chance must be marked down accordingly.

runners_data.name: Katie Can't Count
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and flagged as such — one run returning a fourth on Good is the entire profile; Mullins' second string with Brian Hayes up, and the hurdling headgear note (hg:h) suggests she may have schooling considerations, but a fresh horse from this operation can never be entirely dismissed in a novice.

runners_data.name: Lakewood Rose
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up mare who has placed twice from her last five over similar distances on Good; amateur rider Miss N C Hennessy takes seven pounds which helps the weight, but a winless record over the trip and modest recent form make this more of a frame candidate than a likely winner in most scenarios.

races.paceDynamic: Rosie's Wings is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to press her from the outset, she should be able to dictate a controlled, measured gallop through the early stages of this 2m3f novice hurdle on Good ground. The prominent cluster — Magico, No Mon No Fun, Mino Des Mottes, and La Cote Fleurie — creates genuine congestion for the places immediately behind her, and with four horses chasing two or three positions, traffic friction and bumping for berth between the second and third-last hurdles is a real risk. Eaglewood is a natural prominent type redistributed to midfield here because the field simply cannot accommodate every horse that wants that position, meaning it will likely race further back than ideal and its chance must be assessed accordingly. This race shape — a single unhurried pace-setter and a compressed prominent group — strongly favours horses with tactical versatility and a sharp jump at the last, rewarding the prominent runners who can secure a clean position without burning energy in the early scramble.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rosie's Wings Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Rosie's Wings is allowed to dictate an honest but uncontested gallop and the prominent pack settle without disruption.
scenarios.body: Rosie's Wings sets the fractions from the front and the race unfolds at a rhythm that suits horses travelling smoothly in her wake; horses with a high cruising speed who can match her stride pattern and pounce approaching the last will be best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble Heats Up
scenarios.trigger: If two or more of the prominent group push forward early and force a sharper pace than Rosie's Wings intends to set.
scenarios.body: The elevated tempo fragments the field and increases the chance of errors at hurdles under pressure; horses with a strong staying profile and the ability to absorb a contested early pace before finishing relentlessly will be rewarded.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses from the front and the closers get a dramatic drop in tempo through the back that sets up a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Facile Ocean and Lakewood Rose, tracking from the rear, would be perfectly placed to swoop if the leaders stop in the straight; this scenario demands a genuine change of gear which the Good ground facilitates but the modest pace scenario makes less certain.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Traffic Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the four-horse prominent group collides for position mid-race causing a chain of interference and interference at a crucial hurdle.
scenarios.body: Horses drawn widest or with riders experienced enough to avoid the melee — particularly those sitting just off the pace with room to manoeuvre — benefit most; Katie Can't Count, unknown but lightly raced and fresh, could steal through unhindered if the congestion eliminates rivals.

watchPoints.text: Prominent traffic: Magico, No Mon No Fun, Mino Des Mottes, and La Cote Fleurie all want the same two or three positions behind Rosie's Wings — watch for serious bumping and interference between the third and second-last hurdle as they jostle for berth.

Eaglewood is naturally a prominent racer but is expected to find himself back in midfield; watch whether Phillip Enright pushes forward early regardless, which would further intensify the prominent congestion and heat up the pace.

Katie Can't Count is unknown — one run from the Mullins yard with hurdling headgear noted; watch her schooling before the start and in the early stages for any jumping anxiety that could compromise her or those around her.

La Cote Fleurie returns after 85 days off — watch her in the parade ring and opening stages for any signs of ring rust; if she travels fluently early she is a serious contender, but a stale effort after a layoff cannot be ruled out.

Rosie's Wings controls the tempo entirely — if she quickens approaching the home turn rather than the last, she could steal a march on the prominent pack and make it a test of stamina that suits her more than any of her rivals.

races.name: Tom Lynam Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Cloonainra
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for McConnell who has struggled to recapture form recently (845-07), though has placed at this track on Good; 19 days since last run is fine, but the modest recent record means this is more of an each-way fringe prospect than a leading player.
runners_data.comment: Cloonainra shapes as a leading threat on our rating, which has her nine pounds clear of her official mark, and she has run over today's trip and going before; the concern is that she has been winless in her last five starts, and 166 lb is a hefty burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Magic Day
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's lone front-runner who is tagged as racing slightly out of role as a confirmed pace-setter — O'Keeffe should allow him to bowl along uncontested, but his STYLE_FIT flag means his outright chance is slightly tempered if the race demands a late kick he may not possess.
runners_data.comment: Magic Day comes here in fine heart after finishing second last time out and third three starts back, and with experience of today's distance and going she rates a strong each-way threat at 166 lb — though she remains yet to win in recent starts, which is the lingering concern.

runners_data.name: Mysilverriverfeale
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who won over this exact 19f trip on Good last time out and has placed twice more at similar distances on similar ground; Cooper's yard has limited recent runners (0/2 in 14 days) but this horse arrives in career-best form and the trip-going combination suits well.
runners_data.comment: Mysilverriverfeale won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, but a mark of 106 and a hefty 162 lb burden make her task considerably tougher here, and her overall recent form — a win aside — has been patchy.

runners_data.name: Somersby Roost
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer for McKiernan whose last win came over 19f on Good — pulled up twice since that victory, which is a significant concern, but those runs may have been on unsuitable ground; 42 days off and headgear (t) could sharpen him if the race develops into a stamina test.
runners_data.comment: Somersby Roost has run over today's trip and going, and a win three starts back offers a form lifeline, but consecutive pulled-up efforts last time out and two starts back are impossible to ignore for a mare carrying 162 lb.

runners_data.name: Bhean Saibhre
runners_data.note: Prominent type who won on debut over hurdles but has been placed without winning since, including a second at 18f on Good most recently; five-year-old for Howard who is only 31 days since last run and wears a tongue-tie — consistent place record without winning threatens to continue.
runners_data.comment: Ran well to finish second last time out, but a pulled up three starts back clouds her recent consistency; she has run over today's trip and going, and at 161 lb there is plenty to carry, though an official mark of 105 leaves a little room for optimism.

runners_data.name: Cocovic
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a strong record of placing on Good ground (two seconds at 20f on Good), making the most of a patient ride from O'Brien (5); the absence of a genuine searching pace is the main concern, but if the race does develop into a true test of stamina he has the profile to threaten.
runners_data.comment: Cocovic ran a solid third two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a genuine threat off a mark of 105 with our rating suggesting he holds more in hand than his record implies; the main concern is a 50-day absence.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Place
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-hold-up type who has won twice at 26f on Good, suggesting stamina is his trump card; 42 days since last run and the apparent step back in trip to 2m3f from 3m+ is a query, though Bolger's horses often run well fresh.
runners_data.comment: Pride Of Place shaped well to finish third last time out, with a win three starts back highlighting his class, and experience over today's trip and going works in his favour; the 161 lb burden is the one query, but his rating of 125 marks him as the one to beat in a field of 19.

runners_data.name: Secret Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Collins who won over 16f on Good earlier in the season but steps up markedly in trip here; only 11 days since last run and the jump from 16f to 19f is untested — his form profile at this distance is a genuine unknown.
runners_data.comment: Secret Rock won three starts back but has since disappointed, finishing unplaced and ninth in his last two outings; he has run over today's going before and returns on a quick 11-day turnaround, though his recent downturn makes confidence difficult at 160 lb.

runners_data.name: Emesteraye
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for Ross O'Sullivan who has placed three times in a row at 16f on Good but now faces a significant step up to 2m3f for the first time; the tongue-tie is retained and he clearly goes well on Good, but the unproven stamina at this trip is a material risk.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in her last three starts, Emesteraye arrives here 23 days fresh and has run over today's going before, though she remains yet to win in recent starts and her 159 lb burden is a significant ask against 18 rivals.

runners_data.name: Paul Collins
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for McMahon who placed at 24f on Good last time out — the trip suits but recent form (PP prior to that third) is patchy; 23 days since last run and headgear (p) suggests connections are looking for improvement, and Good ground has been his best surface.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Paul Collins at least showed a flash of form when third two runs back, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions; the 159 lb burden is a stiff ask for a horse whose recent profile is patchy at best.

runners_data.name: Diamond Tipp
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a second at 18f on Good as his best recent effort; Jack Kennedy takes the ride which is a notable booking, and he wears a tongue-tie plus hood — 18 days since last run and the trip-going combination is in range, though his form at 20f on Good is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and with a couple of pulled-up efforts in recent starts, Diamond Tipp faces questions about consistency, though her second last time out and experience over today's trip and going offer some encouragement, and an official rating of 102 gives her a squeak at these weights.

runners_data.name: The Monkey Pole
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed three times at 16-18f on Good without getting his head in front; Condon (5) takes a tricky ride in a congested prominent group and the form suggests he arrives at the track consistently but lacks the acceleration to win — each-way interest at best.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts and having pulled up two runs back, The Monkey Pole faces a stiff ask carrying 158 lb, though a return to third last time out shows some resilience and he has experience of today's trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Parkgarve
runners_data.note: Has won over 18f on Good and placed at 22-23f on Good, making this 19f trip ideal; the yard is in form (2/8 in 14 days) and he has raced 12 of his last 15 starts on Good ground — the most consistently course-and-distance-suited prominent type in the field alongside Blue Reed.
runners_data.comment: Parkgarve has shown only sporadic encouragement in recent starts, finishing out of the frame in three of his last four before that latest win, and ranked fourteenth of nineteen on our figures he faces a stiff task at 155 lb.

runners_data.name: Malikanna
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer for Roche whose best run was a second at 16f on Soft — the redistribution into midfield reflects the congested field rather than his natural inclinations, and on Good ground over 19f he has unproven form; Mark Walsh's presence is the main plus.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, though a second three starts back offers some encouragement; Malikanna has distance and going experience in her favour, but a career-high 153 lb and a ranking of twelfth of nineteen in the field make the challenge substantial.

runners_data.name: Blue Reed
runners_data.note: Has won at 19f on Good and placed at 16-19f on Good repeatedly — the trip-going match is excellent for Collins' horse; consistent placer (four places from last five) who wears a tongue-tie and hood and could be the most likely prominent beneficiary if the race runs to suit.
runners_data.comment: Blue Reed has placed twice in his last five starts, including a runner-up finish last time out, but ranked 15 of 19 on our figures he faces a stiff task at the weights under 151 lb, and the seventh two starts back hints at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Solar Generation
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced five-year-old for Brassil who fades in the finish and is flagged as a true hold-up type squeezed forward by the field's composition; 98 days off is a significant freshness concern, only three career runs, and the fade warning means this race shape is not ideal.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked 17 of 19 on our figures, Solar Generation is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's going before and a return from 98 days off occasionally sparks improvement.

runners_data.name: Kome Dans Un Reve
runners_data.note: Also flagged as fading in the finish and a genuine hold-up type mapped forward against his natural style — 8 days between runs is remarkably quick, and without a jockey name listed the booking is unclear; the fade flag on a 19f Good track is a serious concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Kome Dans Un Reve offers little appeal here — that said, he returns on a quick eight-day turnaround and has run over today's going before, which are about the only positives to cling to.

runners_data.name: Steps In The Sand
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer who is pushed into midfield by the crowded map — Murphy's yard is in form (3/13 in 14 days) and four of his last five runs have been at 18-22f on Good, meaning the trip and ground suit; the STYLE_FIT flag means he may not get the prominent position his form is built on.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, Steps In The Sand faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and her third two starts back shows she can get competitive on her day.

runners_data.name: Andyourbirdcansing
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent type for Ryan whose yard has been quiet (0/20 in 14 days) — also displaced from his natural position by the congested prominent group, and recent form (56510) makes it hard to be enthusiastic; the STYLE_FIT discount applies and the trainer stats are a further concern.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18 of 19 on our figures and returned unplaced last time out, Andyourbirdcansing is hard to fancy with a trainer who has drawn a blank in 20 attempts over the past fortnight; experience over today's trip and going offers some consolation, as does her win two starts back.

races.paceDynamic: Magic Day is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with Darragh O'Keeffe aboard for De Bromhead, is expected to dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good ground — there is no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead, meaning the pace will be honest but controlled rather than pressured or searching. Behind Magic Day, Cloonainra, Mysilverriverfeale, Bhean Saibhre, Pride Of Place, Blue Reed, The Monkey Pole, and Parkgarve all want to race prominently, creating a congested pack that will press forward but is unlikely to force a genuine test of stamina. This race shape — a steady-to-honest pace set by one horse — strongly favours prominent racers who can travel in behind Magic Day, conserve energy through the middle part of the race, and produce a sustained finish from 3 out; hold-up horses dependent on a searching gallop will find themselves covering too much ground for a winning run. The field holds significantly more prominent and hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate in natural positions: Steps In The Sand and Andyourbirdcansing are genuine prominent types who will be squeezed into midfield, while Malikanna, Solar Generation, and Kome Dans Un Reve are true hold-up horses mapped forward — Cloonainra, Blue Reed, and Parkgarve are most likely to secure the prominent slots directly behind Magic Day.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Day sets a measured gallop and the prominent pack tracks without being disrupted, allowing the best-placed prominent runner to pounce from 2 out.
scenarios.body: Magic Day's uncontested lead creates a falsely run or at best honest race, and the horse who travels smoothly in second or third and picks up fluently at the second-last will have a decisive positional edge over hold-up rivals with ground to make up. Prominent types with good course and going form — particularly those who have placed at this trip on Good — are the chief beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Ups Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Day's gallop is genuinely slow and the prominent pack fails to assert, gifting hold-up horses an easier passage to the leaders from 3 out.
scenarios.body: A true crawl would compress the field and strip Magic Day of any advantage, allowing horses like Cocovic, Diamond Tipp, and Somersby Roost to close with purpose from off the pace on the testing final climb. Horses with proven stamina for the 2m3f trip and a good record on Good ground would be best placed to capitalise on rivals who have used energy jostling for position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack pushes up to pressure Magic Day from halfway, turning the race into a genuine stamina test from 3 out.
scenarios.body: A contested pace over this 2m3f trip on Good ground would expose horses with any chink in their stamina, benefiting the most durable stayers who can grind opponents down late. Mysilverriverfeale, with a recent win at the trip on Good, and Pride Of Place, a course specialist at staying trips, would be well-suited to this grind.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaos, Winner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the congested prominent group causes traffic issues or jumping errors that disrupt the race shape entirely, allowing a well-handicapped survivor to profit.
scenarios.body: With so many horses wanting to race in the same space behind Magic Day, bumping, hesitation at hurdles, and interference are genuine risks, and a horse that stays out of trouble on the inner or outer could steal a march on rivals. Parkgarve, who has been in consistent form over this type of trip on Good, and The Monkey Pole, who has placed repeatedly without winning, could benefit from a chaotic race where positional luck matters.

watchPoints.text: Blue Reed and Parkgarve are both natural prominent types with excellent trip-and-going credentials — whichever secures the better position directly behind Magic Day could prove the decisive factor in the finish.

Magic Day's STYLE_FIT flag means O'Keeffe must judge the pace carefully; if he goes too slow, the congested pack behind him risks a scrimmage approaching the first hurdle down the back that could unsettle several runners.

Kome Dans Un Reve has run just 8 days ago and carries a fade-in-finish flag over a trip longer than his proven best — watch for this horse dropping away quickly from 3 out and potentially causing interference.

Jack Kennedy's booking on Diamond Tipp stands out in what looks a moderate handicap — connections may believe the step up beyond 18f on Good suits, and his record of placing suggests he is closer to a win than his form string implies.

Steps In The Sand and Andyourbirdcansing will be unable to get their natural prominent positions in a field this size — watch for both being bustled along early and racing with less fluency than their best form required.

races.name: New Forest Estate & Golf Club Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: One Way Traffic
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Oliver McKiernan, returning after 17 days; best form at 20-25f on Good (sim-going 6/15, one place) and this 26f trip may be at the outer edge of stamina confidence, but the honest pace should suit his style if he travels well.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent if winless in recent starts, One Way Traffic has posted back-to-back runner-up finishes and has run over today's trip and going before, though a hefty 168 lb burden and a ranking of sixth from fourteen suggest he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Gorthill
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for amateur Mr S Connor (7lb claim), trained by Stephen Carlin; excellent sim-going record (9/10 on Good) with one win and three places, and his ability to dictate terms over 22-29f on this surface gives him every chance if Sampoet doesn't match his early pace commitment.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and twice pulled up in that sequence, Gorthill nonetheless carries the weight of a 97-rated performer and our assessment marks him well clear of his rivals; the 19-day turnaround is acceptable, and experience on today's going is at least a known quantity.

runners_data.name: Lecale's Diamond
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator carrying a finish-fade warning for Gavin Cromwell, who is in strong 14-day form (7/20); won at 24f on Good last time and has placed form at this trip, but the late-race stamina concern is real and must be weighed against his solid sim-going record (6/9).|
runners_data.comment: Lecale's Diamond won two starts back but flopped on his most recent outing, and at 165 lb he faces a stiff ask; has run over today's going before, and a trainer striking at 35% recently keeps him of interest despite ranking seventh of fourteen on our ratings.

runners_data.name: Broken Ice
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for John C McConnell running just 6 days after his last start, which is a notably short turnaround; best Good-ground form is placed (sim-going 12/15, one win, two places) and he stays 24f well, but the quick reappearance and modest OR of 93 make him a watch rather than a confident pick.|
runners_data.comment: Broken Ice shaped with plenty of promise when third last time out, and his rating of 102 marks him out as a serious contender in a field of 14; he has run over today's trip and going, and the chief concern is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Sampoet
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner, trained by D M Christie with a 0/1 14-day record; his form string (584U7U) includes two unseats and his sim-going record on Good is modest (13/15, no wins), raising questions about whether he can match Gorthill's stamina and jumping cleanness at this trip.|
runners_data.comment: Sampoet carries a hefty 161 lb yet our rating has him ten points clear of his official mark, making him one to respect despite being winless in his last six; the unseating trouble in recent outings is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Our Zebo
runners_data.note: Long absence of 336 days is the headline concern, but this horse has three wins and seven places on Good going in last 15 runs (sim-going 11/15) and won over 22f at Kilbeggan; if fit enough after the layoff, the honest pace and Good ground are conditions he clearly thrives on.|
runners_data.comment: Our Zebo won two starts back and was third three starts back, showing he can perform at this level, and his distance and going experience stands him in good stead carrying 160 lb; the sole concern is a layoff of 336 days since that latest sixth.

runners_data.name: Zolpharine
runners_data.note: Two recent wins on Good going (22f both times) give Daniel King a genuinely in-form horse to ride, but his true style is hold-up and he is displaced into midfield by the density of non-front-runners; his chance is real if he can access a position closer to his natural race — the style fit (0.92) tempers confidence slightly.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift of the field on our figures and representing a trainer without a winner in 20 recent attempts, Zolpharine is hard to fancy despite back-to-back wins two and three starts back; the hefty 159 lb burden adds further concern.

runners_data.name: Glendine Billy
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the mount for Anthony Mullins after 14 days; a natural hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position given the crowded rear, his recent form (0P9-84) is uninspiring and Good-going record (11/15) is moderate — the style displacement compounds an already difficult profile.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Glendine Billy returns on a quick 14-day turnaround and at least has experience of today's going to call on, though a fourth last time out is the only bright spot in a patchy recent record and his 157 lb burden makes life tough.

runners_data.name: Joe's Turn
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a strong historical record (2 wins, 4 places, 11/15 on Good), but the 40-day absence and the fact he's been bumped forward from his natural rear position by redistribution both work against him; his two wins at 24-25f on Good show the trip and surface are right at least.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked tenth of fourteen on our assessment, Joe's Turn does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, though a fall and a pair of disappointing finishes since a second four starts back make confidence hard to justify at 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: A 13-year-old whose recent form (421321) is astonishingly consistent on Good going (14/15 sim record, 2 wins and 6 places), and while John G Carr's 14-day record is modest (1/8), this horse outperforms his OR=81; naturally a hold-up horse shifted forward on the map, but his relentless finishing record makes him dangerous regardless of positional noise.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked a lowly 13 of 14 on our figures, Fr Gilligansvoyge faces a stiff ask under 151 lb, yet there is genuine recent form to note — a winner last time out and a second two starts back, with experience of today's distance and going in his favour.

runners_data.name: Seventy Eight Team
runners_data.note: The one genuine prominent-style horse behind the two front-runners, giving Danny Gilligan a tactical option to track the pace and be delivered at the right moment; Paul John Gilligan's 14-day record is 0/10, which is a negative trainer angle, and the form (45P-P8) doesn't inspire confidence at this trip.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, including two pulled-up efforts, Seventy Eight Team faces a stiff ask off 149 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 86 suggests some latent ability to tap into.

runners_data.name: Deadheat
runners_data.note: Aged 13 and returning after 49 days, this horse is a true hold-up type mapped to midfield; his Good-going sim record is limited (4/15) and recent form (79/P-0) is deeply unconvincing — the style displacement only adds to what is already a very difficult profile to recommend.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and pulled up two runs back, Deadheat arrives on 49 days off carrying 148 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 96 suggests more ability than his official mark of 78 implies.

runners_data.name: He Fitz In
runners_data.note: Not run for 197 days and wears a visor; a hold-up operator by nature, his entire recent form string (66766) shows consistent mid-pack finishes and his sim-going record on Good (9/15) is patchy — the lengthy absence and lack of any recent Good-ground form make him a significant risk.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and not seen on a racecourse for 197 days, He Fitz In has run over today's distance and going before but has been out of the frame throughout recent starts, and at 148 lb he faces a stiff task from 11th in the rankings.

runners_data.name: Tullabrack Lad
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old returning after 131 days carrying a finish-fade warning and the lowest OR in the field (72); a hold-up horse naturally pushed forward on the map, and his form on Good (7/14 sim) along with a 5-pound claim for Michael Kenneally don't compensate for the stamina concern and layoff combination.|
runners_data.comment: Tullabrack Lad has been winless in his last four starts, with a pulled-up effort among them, and our figures rank him last of the field; 131 days off the track adds to the concerns, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Gorthill and Sampoet are the two confirmed front-runners in this 14-runner field over 3m2f at Kilbeggan on Good ground, and both are likely to contest the early lead, creating a genuine and honest gallop from the outset rather than a false or dawdling pace. Seventy Eight Team will look to slot into a prominent position behind them, while One Way Traffic, Lecale's Diamond, Broken Ice, and Our Zebo are the primary hold-up operators who will need the pace to be sustained to deliver their finishing efforts. The field carries significantly more hold-up and midfield types than can all race at the rear in their natural position — Zolpharine, Glendine Billy, Joe's Turn, Fr Gilligansvoyge, Deadheat, He Fitz In, and Tullabrack Lad are all genuine back-of-the-field horses who will be compressed into midfield, meaning the bunch is denser in the middle sections than the map suggests. With a genuine two-horse duel up front over a stamina trip on Good ground, this race shape most favours proven stayers who can travel mid-to-rear and pick off a tiring front rank in the final mile — the hold-up profile is the dominant beneficiary, provided those horses have authentic finishing ability at this trip and going.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Stayers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Gorthill and Sampoet share a genuine gallop throughout, emptying early and leaving the race open for closers in the final mile.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other out over the gruelling 3m2f trip on Good ground, creating an honest tempo that suits genuine staying hold-up types who have been travelling comfortably behind them. Horses with strong sim-going records on Good and proven stamina at this distance are best placed to swoop; Our Zebo, Lecale's Diamond, and One Way Traffic are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Contest
scenarios.trigger: If one of Gorthill or Sampoet dominates or the other capitulates early, allowing the survivor to establish a rhythm and control the pace.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner settling into their own rhythm at an honest but manageable gallop over this extreme trip can be very hard to catch, particularly if the hold-up pack is compressed and disorganised in midfield. Gorthill has strong sim-going form (9/10 Good) and solid place record over fences, making him the more likely candidate to capitalise if Sampoet fades or blunders.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Find Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield creates traffic problems for the true hold-up runners and a prominent-tracking type emerges with a clear run.
scenarios.body: With so many horses squeezed into the middle section of the race, those mapped to midfield but capable of staying on powerfully — particularly Fr Gilligansvoyge, whose form string (421321) is relentlessly consistent on Good — can thread through a tiring field if they get a clean passage. Zolpharine, with two recent wins on Good going, also has the form to capitalise if racing in a role closer to its natural tempo than its redistribution suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Crawl, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If neither Gorthill nor Sampoet fully commits to the pace and the gallop is surprisingly moderate for the early stages.
scenarios.body: A false or muddling pace over 3m2f on Good ground would compress the field and produce a scramble from home, favouring horses sharp enough to quicken off a slower tempo — a scenario that suits fresh legs and horses with tactical speed rather than pure staying ability. This is the least likely shape given the presence of two genuine front-runners, but a blunder or error from either early could briefly scramble the order.

watchPoints.text: Sampoet's jumping reliability is a serious concern — two unseats (U) in recent form over fences at this distance means he represents a real race-interference risk if he makes a jumping error while sharing the early lead with Gorthill, potentially causing disruption to the prominent and midfield groups.|

Our Zebo is unraced for 336 days and, while his Good-ground form at Kilbeggan is strong (3 wins, 7 places), connections need to be confident he has returned fit — watch him in the paddock and early in the race for signs of rustiness that could compromise what is otherwise an ideal profile.|

The compressed midfield — caused by seven hold-up types being pushed forward — creates a genuine traffic and scrimmaging risk from the early fences onward; horses on the inner, particularly those without natural jumping fluency, could be in trouble if the field concertinas behind the pace.|

Fr Gilligansvoyge's consistent form (421321) at OR=81 is the kind of angle that can be overlooked in a field this deep, and at 13 years old he continues to run to a level well above his official rating on Good going — his finishing efforts late in races warrant attention even if his redistribution map position isn't ideal.|

Gorthill's amateur rider (Mr S Connor, 7lb claim) is a factor to monitor — the 7lb allowance is valuable in a handicap, but front-runners ridden by claimer-class jockeys over 26 fences at 3m2f are vulnerable to pace-judgement errors in the final circuit, which could undermine what is otherwise a strong profile for the likely dominant shape.|

races.name: Belvedere House & Gardens Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Charlie Luciano
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator for Noel Meade who won over 2m on good ground 21 days ago; his recent handicap form shows inconsistency at longer trips but good-ground figures are solid across 14 of 15 career runs, and the 7lb claimer Mr D McGill adds some weight relief.
runners_data.comment: Charlie Luciano won two starts back and returns here on a workable 21-day break, with experience of both today's trip and conditions in his favour; the 166 lb burden is the main question mark, but his recent winning form makes him our preferred selection.

runners_data.name: A Wave Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up type returning after 67 days off for J P Broderick; has placed twice from 12 good-ground runs but has not won at this trip level recently, and the layoff combined with a 3m2f stamina test on good ground is a mild concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and off the track for 67 days, A Wave Of The Sea nonetheless has run over today's going before, and he tops our figures here — though a seventh last time out raises questions about current form.

runners_data.name: Ceanndana
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a tongue-tie fitted, trained by Ross O'Sullivan and ridden by the reliable Keith Donoghue; ran just 13 days ago and finished fourth over 2m4f on good ground, and his record of four wins from 13 good-ground starts makes him a natural fit for this surface and pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ceanndana arrives here on a 13-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going in his favour, and a third three starts back offers some encouragement, though 162 lb is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Koori Star
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Peter Fahey, but the STYLE_FIT flag indicates he is racing in a field where his lead is unchallenged — which is a double-edged sword; his recent form reads nine runs without a win or place on good going, and his sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from eight comparable runs is the most damning statistic in the field.
runners_data.comment: Koori Star has experience of today's trip and conditions and, rated 116, he shapes as a leading threat from a compact 20-day turnaround, but the main concern is his winless recent record — ninth last time out and struggling to convert in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Ira Hayes
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a visor fitted for John McConnell, who is in strong form at 3/28 over 14 days; won 22 days ago over 2m2f on good ground and ran second at 3m on the same surface — the trip-and-going combination is a genuine fit, and Michael Kenneally's 5lb claim keeps the weight competitive.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures and yet to threaten in his last two starts, Ira Hayes faces a stiff ask here, though a win and a second in recent starts show he retains ability, and he has experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Scalpnagoon
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old has a tongue-tie on and Jack Kennedy in the saddle, which immediately raises the profile; has placed in seven of 11 career runs on good ground including multiple seconds and thirds, never won at 3m2f but the relentless placed consistency suggests a horse who finds his level and runs to it every time.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and lightly raced on the figures, Scalpnagoon has finished placed in five of his last six starts, including a second two starts back and a third last time out over today's trip and going, arriving here fit on a 13-day turnaround; the risk is he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Granville Street
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Ciaran Murphy who has placed twice from seven good-ground starts; his historic distance profile shows most runs at well below 3m2f, and the step up in trip to the longest test of his career is the primary concern for Eoin Walsh navigating Kilbeggan's idiosyncratic track.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and a pulled-up effort lurking in recent form, Granville Street does at least return on a quick turnaround of 20 days with going experience in his favour, though 157 lb is a stern ask for a horse yet to find his best.

runners_data.name: Ad Caelum
runners_data.note: Won a 3m chase on good ground in his last victory and carries genuine closer credentials — his natural style is hold-up racing, but the map places him in midfield because the field has more rear-runners than positions; J J Slevin is a major positive and the 0/20 trainer form over 14 days is worth noting as a mild dampener on confidence.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time out is the blot that dominates Ad Caelum's profile, and with her trainer winless in 20 attempts over the past fortnight and our rating ranking her eighth of nine, she faces a stiff task, though she has experience over today's trip and going and did score three starts back.

runners_data.name: The Dara Man
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old whose recent form includes two pulls-up and a fall — jumping reliability is a significant concern at 3m2f; a natural hold-up operator placed in midfield on the map due to field congestion at the rear, and his sim-going record of zero wins from 12 comparable runs underlines that a big run would require everything to go right.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, The Dara Man's recent record — featuring two pull-ups and a fall — makes him very hard to fancy, though he has run over today's going before and returns on a reasonable freshener of 35 days.

races.paceDynamic: Koori Star is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 3m2f handicap chase on Good ground at Kilbeggan, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Danny Gilligan can dictate a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front. The pace is likely to be honest but controlled — 3m2f on good ground over fences demands a steady clip, but without pressure Koori Star can conserve energy through the early stages before the race ignites from three out. Ceanndana, Ira Hayes, and Scalpnagoon are the prominent stalkers who will track the leader and be best placed to pounce if Koori Star's stamina is tested late; this shape strongly favours prominent-to-handy runners who travel into the race without burning fuel in a scrimmage. This field contains more hold-up types than the map can seat at the rear — Ad Caelum and The Dara Man are genuine closers shuffled to midfield on the map because the hold-up berths are over-subscribed, but Ceanndana, Ira Hayes, and Scalpnagoon are best positioned to exploit a controlled pace with a clean passage into the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Koori Star sets a controlled pace and the prominent trio of Ceanndana, Ira Hayes, and Scalpnagoon travel smoothly in his wake before pressing from three out.
scenarios.body: The steady gallop suits horses who can sit handy without burning energy, and the trio have the class, form on good ground, and tactical positions to challenge powerfully from the final turn; Ceanndana's recent course experience and Scalpnagoon's relentless placed form are particularly well-suited.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Koori Star's rider successfully slows the pace to a crawl early, conserves energy jumping well, and kicks decisively from two out before rivals can close.
scenarios.body: An uncontested, slow-burn gallop over 3m2f can produce a leader who finds more in the tank than expected when rivals are still working to close; at OR 115 Koori Star has the rating to be competitive if the race is run entirely to his terms.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected in the middle stages and the prominent runners are used up, creating a genuine closing opportunity from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Charlie Luciano showed a good win on good ground over 2m on similar recent form, and A Wave Of The Sea has placed credentials at this trip on good ground; however, this scenario is tempered by the fact that true hold-up running requires a genuinely strong early pace that this field shape is unlikely to generate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Errors Disrupt
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or a mid-race incident among the prominent runners causes reshuffling and an unconventional finish.
scenarios.body: Kilbeggan's tight, undulating track punishes errors at pace, and in a 9-runner handicap over 3m2f with several horses with question marks in form — The Dara Man's recent falls and Koori Star's STYLE_FIT flag — untidy jumping could compromise the race shape entirely; Ad Caelum, who won on good ground at 3m, could benefit from a scrambled finish.

watchPoints.text: Koori Star's jumping must be monitored from flag-fall — if he makes an early error and loses the lead, no other runner is mapped to take it up and the race shape could become chaotic.

The Dara Man's recent run of falls and pull-ups (form: PP-83F) makes him a live risk at Kilbeggan's fences; connections and punters should note Daniel King has limited cover if this horse meets a fence wrong.
Scalpnagoon's consistent placing record masks that he has not yet won at 3m2f — watch whether Jack Kennedy rides him aggressively enough to force a win rather than settling for another place finish.

Ad Caelum and The Dara Man are both shown in midfield but are genuine closers by nature — if the pace is softer than expected, watch for them drifting even further back and losing all hope of making a meaningful challenge.

Ira Hayes is only 19 days off a win and carries a visor; trainer John McConnell's 3/28 14-day strike rate is the best in the field — watch for this horse to be produced with a well-timed run off the prominent pace.

races.name: John Thomas McNamara Series Flat Race

runners_data.name: Bellahill
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 6yo (509 days off) with just one run to reference — S R B Crawford stable has had no winners in 14 days; style entirely unknown, making her a wildcard who could settle anywhere in the pack.|
runners_data.comment: Bellahill returns from a 509-day absence carrying 168 lb, but he shaped with promise when third last time out and remains unexposed, leaving plenty of room for improvement on his limited showing.

runners_data.name: Blackwood Joe
runners_data.note: 5yo with a single run on similar Good ground, finished a distant last (17/18f); has a fade-in-finish flag and returns after just 18 days, suggesting connections are persisting despite that debut disappointment.|
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Blackwood Joe returns after 18 days carrying 168 lb and, though yet to win in recent starts, his lightly raced profile leaves plenty to work with.

runners_data.name: In Around Thehouse
runners_data.note: 467 days absent and fell on last start — enormous question marks over fitness and confidence; jockey Barnett claims a 2lb allowance which helps but the layoff and fall make this a significant risk in an 11-runner bumper.|
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, In Around Thehouse returns from a 467-day absence having fallen on his sole recent start, carrying 168 lb as he bids to show what he's capable of on a comeback that leaves plenty of questions unanswered.

runners_data.name: Long Story
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who has posted three 7th-or-worse finishes on Good ground, suggesting straightforward form but not enough top-end finish; Halford's 2lb claim could help in a stamina-test scenario if the pace collapses.|
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Long Story has been finding things tough in his last three starts but remains lightly raced and capable of better; yet to win, he carries 168 lb on a 31-day break and could still have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Ddakji
runners_data.note: True hold-up type by inclination mapped to midfield here because the rear is overcrowded — fades in finishes and has two placeless runs on similar Going; the positional compromise means his natural closing style is further blunted in this race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Ddakji arrives here 25 days fresh, has run over today's trip, and our rating of 68 puts him third of eleven in the field; the risk is that a ninth-place finish last time out leaves him needing a sharp upturn on recent form to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Hill Silver
runners_data.note: Ciaran Murphy's yard has been active (3/13 in 14 days) and this 4yo has posted back-to-back 4th-place finishes on Good ground showing consistency — although a natural closer, the redistribution to midfield means he cannot fully deploy his preferred come-from-behind approach.|
runners_data.comment: Hill Silver has run over today's trip and arrives here in decent nick after 25 days off, with his speed rating of 93 giving him a strong case as the chief danger to the top-rated runner; the risk is that he remains winless in his last two starts.

runners_data.name: Lone Ash Lad
runners_data.note: Debutant 4yo with no public form or last-run data available — complete unknown whose chances depend entirely on home homework; if unexposed and well-schooled, the bumper format gives him a clean canvas.|
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Lone Ash Lad is yet to score under rules and arrives as an unknown quantity, but that lightly raced profile leaves plenty of room for improvement as he steps out carrying 165 lb.

runners_data.name: Reafadda
runners_data.note: One bumper run (6th, 16f, Good) represents thin evidence; John Patrick Ryan's yard has had no runners in 14 days and this 4yo's hold-up style means he needs a faster gallop than Baymount is likely to provide to make an impact.|
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and unexposed, Reafadda is yet to score in recent starts but remains open to improvement; the yard is without a return from its last 20 runners over a fortnight, and 165 lb is a stern ask as he bids to build on that sixth.

runners_data.name: A Quest For Cognac
runners_data.note: Prominent type who fades in finishes and ran 14th on the only comparable Good-ground run; hood fitted (hg:h) may help concentration but the fade flag limits confidence if he does press Baymount into an honest pace — likely to set up the race for others.|
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, A Quest For Cognac has shown limited recent form — unplaced before a fall — yet to win in her last two starts, though carrying 161 lb she merits respect as a lightly raced mare with more to offer.

runners_data.name: Baymount
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner who comes here on a short 14-day turnaround; Anthony Mullins yard has had a winner recently, and on Good Kilbeggan turf over 2m Hendrick will be able to control tempo — the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild caution but his natural role is uncontested here.|
runners_data.comment: Baymount has run over today's trip and going before, and a third last time out — after two pulled-up efforts — suggests she is returning to form at the right moment; winless in her last four, the weight is a notable ask at 161 lb, but her rating heads the field.

runners_data.name: No Brainer
runners_data.note: Fitted with a tongue-strap (tp), 36 days off, and a P-P-0 recent form string — three placeless runs with a fade-in-finish pattern; Ms Persse's 4lb claim helps weight but the form profile in a field where the pace is likely to be conservative is uninspiring.|
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to score, No Brainer returns after 36 days carrying 161 lb, and with two pull-ups in her recent record she faces questions on that front, though her lightly raced profile leaves room for better.

races.paceDynamic: Baymount is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner bumper and will look to control proceedings from the outset, with A Quest For Cognac likely to press or sit just off the pace in a prominent berth. On Good ground over 2m at Kilbeggan, Baymount can dictate a sustainable, unhurried gallop that plays directly to his strengths — there is no rival with confirmed early pace to pressurise him into going too fast. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Hill Silver and Ddakji are genuine closers by inclination but are shown in midfield because the rear positions are overcrowded, meaning their true finishing kick may be partially compromised by position. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a controlled tempo on Good turf — strongly favours horses who can track the pace closely and sustain their effort through the straight, rewarding prominent or close-tracking profiles over pure hold-up types who need a strong gallop to reel in the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Baymount Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Baymount secures the lead uncontested and controls a measured pace throughout the 2m trip.
scenarios.body: Baymount can bowl along in front without any rival willing or able to pressurise him, conserving enough energy to kick again inside the final furlong; Anthony Mullins's yard has had a winner in the last 14 days and Hendrick is an experienced amateur in these bumpers. A Quest For Cognac and any horse able to sit close in the prominent zone benefit most from not having to make up ground against a fresh, unextended front-runner.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Late
scenarios.trigger: If Baymount's early control produces a slow enough gallop that energy-rich hold-up types arrive with a late surge.
scenarios.body: A collapse or weakening from the prominent horses in the final 2f would open a gap for the closest-tracking midfield horses to finish strongly on the Good ground; Hill Silver's two consecutive 4th-place finishes on similar going suggest consistent improvement without winning, but a true solo pace could finally suit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Rival Challenges
scenarios.trigger: If A Quest For Cognac or an unknown-style runner forces the pace and turns this into a genuine contest for the lead.
scenarios.body: A contested pace would stretch the field earlier than Baymount wants, potentially exposing the front-runner late and creating opportunity for a prominent horse with better stamina reserves to take over; A Quest For Cognac does fade in finishes so this scenario may not suit the challenger itself, opening the door for a tracking horse.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Bumper Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of unknown and lightly-raced horses creates early interference and disrupts normal running order.
scenarios.body: Several runners — Bellahill, In Around Thehouse, Lone Ash Lad — have significant gaps since last run or minimal form evidence, and a muddled bumper pace could randomise the result; lightly-raced unexposed types then become live factors regardless of conventional style classification.

watchPoints.text: Baymount is the only confirmed front-runner — watch whether Hendrick is allowed to bowl along unchallenged from flag-fall or if A Quest For Cognac's jockey Walsh tests him for the lead in the early stages, as that dynamic decides the entire race shape.

A Quest For Cognac has a fade-in-finish flag and a hood — if Walsh pushes forward and takes it to Baymount, monitor whether he cries enough in the final 2f to create a gap for trailing horses that would not otherwise have had the pace to exploit.

Hill Silver and Ddakji are both genuine hold-up types forced into midfield by field congestion — watch their early position; if either secures a true rear berth, their late-run potential increases, but if trapped in traffic mid-pack their redistributed role blunts their chance.

In Around Thehouse (467-day absence, previous fall) and Bellahill (509-day absence) are significant behavioural risks in the early stages — either could cause interference or break the race rhythm unpredictably in the first half-mile of this bumper.

Lone Ash Lad is an unraced debutant with no form data — if showing unexpected natural speed or a prominent position from the gate, reassess the pace scenario immediately as he could unexpectedly push Baymount along.
